facts.statement: The type species Dromaeosaurus albertensis was described by William Diller Matthew and Barnum Brown in 1922.
facts.quote: The type species is Dromaeosaurus albertensis, which was described by William Diller Matthew and Barnum Brown in 1922.

facts.statement: The first Dromaeosaurus remains were found by Barnum Brown in 1914 near the Red Deer River in Alberta.
facts.quote: The first known Dromaeosaurus remains were discovered by paleontologist Barnum Brown during a 1914 expedition to Red Deer River on behalf of the American Museum of Natural History.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen AMNH 5356 includes a partial skull measuring 24 cm in length, a lower jaw, hyoid bones, a metacarpal, and foot bones.
facts.quote: The find, holotype AMNH 5356, consisted of a partial skull 24 cm in length, a mandible, two hyoids, a first metacarpal and some foot bones.

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus had a heavy build, making it sturdier than similarly sized dromaeosaurids like Velociraptor.
facts.quote: Dromaeosaurus was heavily built, more so than other dromaeosaurids that are similar in size, like Velociraptor.

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus was a medium-sized carnivore reaching about 2 meters in length and weighing 16 kilograms.
facts.quote: Dromaeosaurus was a medium-sized carnivore, about 2 m in length and 16 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus had only nine teeth in each upper jaw.
facts.quote: It had only nine teeth in each maxilla.

facts.statement: Researchers estimated Dromaeosaurus had a bite nearly three times stronger than Velociraptor's, suggesting it relied more on its jaws than its sickle claw for killing prey.
facts.quote: Therrien et al. (2005) estimated that Dromaeosaurus had a bite nearly three times as powerful as that of Velociraptor and suggested it relied more on its jaws than on the sickle claw to kill its prey.

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus used a characteristic "puncture and pull" feeding method typical of coelurosaurian theropods.
facts.quote: Dromaeosaurus feeding habits were also discovered to be typical of coelurosaurian theropods, with a characteristic "puncture and pull" feeding method.

facts.statement: Studies suggest Dromaeosaurus included bone in its diet and was better adapted to attack struggling prey compared to troodontids that ate softer animals and carrion.
facts.quote: The same study also indicated that both Dromaeosaurus and Saurornitholestes (also analyzed in the study) likely included bone in their diet and were better adapted to handle the stresses associated with attacking struggling prey while troodontids, equipped with weaker jaws, preyed on softer animals and prey items such as invertebrates and carrion.

facts.statement: In 1969, John H. Ostrom assigned Dromaeosaurus to the family Dromaeosauridae based on shared features with Velociraptor and Deinonychus.
facts.quote: In 1969, John H. Ostrom recognized that Dromaeosaurus shared many features with Velociraptor and the newly discovered Deinonychus, and assigned these forms to a new family: Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: The exact evolutionary relationships of Dromaeosaurus remain somewhat unclear among scientists.
facts.quote: The exact relationships of Dromaeosaurus are somewhat unclear.

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus had large teeth shaped like curved cones covered in enamel.
facts.quote: Its teeth were rather large and were shaped like a curved cone with a coat of enamel covering the crown.

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus had a vein at the back of its head called the vena capitis dorsalis that drained neck muscles through canals to the brain.
facts.quote: Dromaeosaurus also had a vein at the back of the head, the vena capitis dorsalis, that drained the front neck muscles through two long canals running to the posterior surface of the brain.

facts.statement: Despite popular casts in museums worldwide, Dromaeosaurus is actually poorly known from real fossil evidence.
facts.quote: Despite receiving widespread attention in popular books on dinosaurs, and the usage of a complete mounted skeleton cast in museums throughout the world, Dromaeosaurus is poorly known from actual fossils.

facts.statement: Teeth attributed to Dromaeosaurus have been found in the Prince Creek Formation.
facts.quote: Teeth attributed to this genus have been found in the Prince Creek Formation.

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, between 80 and 69 million years ago, from the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico Superior, entre 80 a 69 millones de años, entre el Campaniano al Maastrichtiano

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus lived in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus was a fast predator the size of a wolf, measuring around 1.80 to 2 meters in length and weighing about 15 kilograms.
facts.quote: Dromaeosaurus, era un rápido depredador de tamaño equivalente a un lobo, medía alrededor de 1,80 a 2 metros de longitud y pesaba unos 15 kilogramos

facts.statement: According to 2007 studies by Therner and Henderson estimating weight based on skull length, Dromaeosaurus weighed 16.29 kilograms.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con los estudios de Therner y Henderson en 2007, en los que el peso de los terópodos se estimó en función de la longitud del cráneo, el Dromaeosaurus pesó 16,29 kilogramos

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus had a mouth full of sharp teeth and a strongly curved sickle claw on each foot.
facts.quote: Su boca estaba llena de dientes afilados, y tenía una "garra de hoz" fuertemente curvada en cada pie

facts.statement: In Dromaeosaurus, the sickle claw was of intermediate size compared to other dromaeosaurids and would have been used to grip prey and inflict serious wounds.
facts.quote: En Dromaeosaurus esta es de tamaño intermedio comparada con la de otros dromeosáuridos y le serviría para aferrarse a sus presas causándoles graves heridas

facts.statement: The sickle claw on the second toe of Dromaeosaurus was longer than 7.5 centimeters.
facts.quote: Una garra en el segundo dedo del pie tenía una longitud de más de 7,5 centímetros

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus walked on the outer edges of its feet, lifting the other toes to protect its large, sickle-clawed claws.
facts.quote: Dromaeosaurus caminaba con los lados externos de los pies y levantaron los otros dedos, protegiendo así las garras grandes y dotadas de hoz

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus had forelimbs that could move like human arms due to their joint construction and ended in sharp claws.
facts.quote: Otra arma de estos dinosaurios eran sus extremidades anteriores, que gracias a la construcción de las articulaciones podían moverse como los humanos, y que también terminaban con afiladas garras

facts.statement: Tests by Therrien, Ruff, and Henderson in 2005 showed that Dromaeosaurus had a grip bite force three times greater than that of the similarly sized dinosaur Velociraptor.
facts.quote: Las pruebas de Therrien, Ruff y Henderson 2005 mostraron que Dromaeosaurus tendría mordidas de sujeción con una fuerza que es tres veces mayor que la del dinosaurio de tamaño similar Velociraptor

facts.statement: The skull of Dromaeosaurus differed from other dromaeosaurids by being short and solid, resembling a miniature Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Dromaeosaurus difiere de otros dromeosáuridos por ser corto y macizo lo que le hace parecer un Tyrannosaurus en miniatura

facts.statement: Behind its eye sockets, Dromaeosaurus had a structure crossing the skull like a hinge that would act as a shock absorber to protect the brain during bites.
facts.quote: Tras las órbitas tenía una estructura que cruza el cráneo en forma de bisagra que serviría de parachoques para protegerse de lesiones cerebrales durante la dentellada

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus had notably large eyes, suggesting it possessed excellent vision.
facts.quote: Dromaeosaurus tenía unos ojos notablemente grandes lo que lleva a pensar que poseía una excelente visión

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus probably had a keen sense of smell and hearing.
facts.quote: También probablemente tenía gran sentido del olfato y oído

facts.statement: The tail of Dromaeosaurus was flexible at the base but reinforced by a lattice of bony bars that allowed it to be held raised in an acute upward position.
facts.quote: La cola era flexible en la base pero fue unida por un enrejado de barras óseas que permitía que fuera llevada levantada en una posición aguda hacia arriba

facts.statement: The tail of Dromaeosaurus was rigid except at the base, with thin, flexible bone rods that likely acted as a rudder to help change direction quickly during a run and maintain flight trajectory during a jump toward prey.
facts.quote: La cola de estos dinosaurios estaba rígida, flexible solo en la base, con varillas de hueso delgadas y flexibles, probablemente se utilizó como timón que lo ayudó a cambiar rápidamente la dirección de la carrera y mantuvo la trayectoria de vuelo durante el salto hacia la víctima

facts.statement: It is very likely that Dromaeosaurus was covered in feathers, as has been proven in other dromaeosaurids like Velociraptor or Microraptor.
facts.quote: es muy probable que los Dromaeosaurus estuvieran cubiertos de plumas como ya se ha podido probar en otros dromeosáuridos como Velociraptor o Microraptor

facts.statement: D. albertensis was discovered in 1914 by fossil hunter Barnum Brown near the Red Deer River in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: D. albertensis fue descubierto en 1914 por el conocido buscador de fósiles Barnum Brown en las proximidades del río Red Deer en el territorio de Alberta, Canadá

facts.statement: The initial discovery consisted of a partial skull about 22 centimeters long and leg bones.
facts.quote: El hallazgo consistía en un cráneo parcial de alrededor de 22 centímetros de largo y huesos de las patas

facts.statement: The holotype specimen AMNH 5356 consisted of a partial skull 24 centimeters long, a jaw, two hyoids, a first metacarpal, and some foot bones.
facts.quote: El hallazgo, holotipo AMNH 5356, consistía en un cráneo parcial de 24 centímetros de longitud, una mandíbula, dos hioides, un primer metacarpiano y algunos huesos del pie

facts.statement: The area where these bones were collected is now part of the Dinosaur Provincial Park in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: El área donde se recogieron estos huesos es ahora parte del Parque provincial de los Dinosaurios en Alberta, Canadá

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus albertensis is the type specimen and the most complete known member of the genus, and the family dromaeosaurids is named after it.
facts.quote: Dromaeosaurus albertensis es el espécimen tipo y el más completo que se conoce del género y por él también se nombra a toda la familia, los dromeosáuridos

facts.statement: Due to the fragmentary nature of the fossil material, only the type species D. albertensis is considered valid.
facts.quote: Debido a la naturaleza fragmentaria del material fósil, solo la especie tipo D. albertensis es considerada válida

facts.statement: The generic name Dromaeosaurus derives from the Greek words dromeus meaning 'runner' and sauros meaning 'lizard'.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del griego δρομεύς, dromeus que significa "corredor" y σαύρος, sauros que significa "lagarto"

facts.statement: Despite popular media attention, Dromaeosaurus is known from surprisingly few actual fossils.
facts.quote: Dromaeosaurus se conoce asombrosamente por pocos fósiles reales

facts.statement: Matthew and Brown originally classified Dromaeosaurus in the subfamily Dromaeosaurinae within the family Deinodontidae, now known as Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: Matthew y Brown originalmente colocaron Dromaeosaurus en su propia subfamilia, los Dromaeosaurinae, dentro de los "Deinodontidae", ahora conocidos como Tyrannosauridae

facts.statement: In 1969, John H. Ostrom recognized that Dromaeosaurus shared many characteristics with Velociraptor and Deinonychus and assigned these forms to the new family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: En 1969, John H. Ostrom reconoció que Dromaeosaurus compartía muchas características con Velociraptor y el recientemente descubierto Deinonychus y asignó estas formas a una nueva familia, Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: Recently, the genus Dakotaraptor has been classified as the sister taxon to Dromaeosaurus.
facts.quote: Desde hace poco, el género Dakotaraptor ha sido clasificado como el taxón hermano de Dromaeosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2015 analysis by paleontologists Robert DePalma, David Burnham, Larry Martin, Peter Larson, and Robert Bakker classified Dromaeosaurus as the sister taxon to Dakotaraptor.
facts.quote: El siguiente cladograma sigue un análisis de 2015 de los paleontólogos Robert DePalma, David Burnham, Larry Martin , Peter Larson y Robert Bakker , utilizando datos actualizados del Grupo de Trabajo Theropod. En este análisis, Dromaeosaurus se clasifica como el taxón hermano de Dakotaraptor.

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus differs from most relatives by having a short, massive skull, a deep jaw, and robust teeth.
facts.quote: Dromaeosaurus se diferencia de la mayoría de sus parientes en tener un cráneo corto, masivo, una mandíbula profunda y dientes robustos.

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus had notably large eyes providing good vision, along with well-developed smell and hearing.
facts.quote: Sus ojos eran notablemente grandes lo que le proporcionaría un buen sentido de la vista, poseyendo además olfato y oído muy desarrollados.

facts.statement: Its rigid tail allowed Dromaeosaurus to maintain balance while running at speeds over 40 km/h.
facts.quote: si debía perseguir a sus presas su cola rígida le permitiría mantener el equilibrio en la carrera pudiendo correr a más de 40 km/h.

facts.statement: Therrien et al. in 2005 estimated that Dromaeosaurus had a bite nearly three times more powerful than that of Velociraptor.
facts.quote: Therrien et al. en 2005 estimaron que Dromaeosaurus tenía una mordedura casi tres veces más poderosa que la del Velociraptor

facts.statement: The discovery of the sister species Dakotaraptor, which has a larger flexor tubercle than most other dromaeosaurids, supports the suggestion that Dromaeosaurus used its sickle claw less than other dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de la especie hermana Dakotaraptor, que tiene un tubérculo flexor mayor que la mayoría de los otros dromeosáuridos, también respalda la sugerencia de que Dromaeosaurus habría usado su garra falciforme menos que otros dromeosáuridos.

facts.statement: Studies of tooth wear patterns by Angélica Torices et al. indicate that dromaeosaurid teeth share wear patterns similar to those observed in tyrannosaurids and troodontids, respectively.
facts.quote: Estudios de patrones de desgaste en los dientes de este animal por Angélica Torices et al. en un estudio sobre los hábitos de alimentación de los terópodos, indican que los dientes de los dromeosáuridos comparten patrones de desgaste similares a los observados en los tiranosáuridos y los troodóntidos, respectivamente.

facts.statement: The same study indicated that both Dromaeosaurus and Saurornitholestes likely included bone in their diet.
facts.quote: El mismo estudio también indicó que tanto Dromaeosaurus como Saurornitholestes, también analizados en el estudio, probablemente incluyeron hueso en su dieta

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus lived from the Albian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 110.1 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Maastrichtian (110.1 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Dromaeosaurus was named by Matthew and Brown in 1922.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Dromaeosaurus (genus), Matthew and Brown 1922

facts.statement: There are 48 recorded fossil occurrences of Dromaeosaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 48

facts.statement: It is debated whether the unusual, grooved "Dromaeosaurus morphotype A" teeth found in Alberta belong to Dromaeosaurus, as their origin remains confusing.
facts.quote: "Dromaeosaurus morfotipo A" es la designación dada a una serie de dientes inusuales, surcados de Alberta. Estos dientes no pertenecen probablemente a Dromaeosaurus, aunque sea confuso de qué animal vienen.

facts.statement: The exact relationships of Dromaeosaurus are unclear, and it is debated whether its robust construction makes it appear primitive despite being a highly specialized animal.
facts.quote: Las relaciones exactas de Dromaeosaurus son poco claras. Aunque su construcción robusta le da una apariencia primitiva, en realidad era un animal muy especializado.

facts.statement: Dromaeosaurus could hunt prey similar to or larger than itself, such as ornithomimids, ornithopods, and juvenile ceratopsians, while not ignoring smaller prey like lizards and mammals.
facts.quote: pudiendo dar caza a presas de tamaño similar o mayor a él como ornitomímidos, ornitópodos y ceratopsianos jóvenes, aunque no desdeñaría presas más pequeñas como lagartos y mamíferos.
